title: S026 — Phase-A reconsideration semantics / sound invalidation boundary
description: Characterise exactly what causes a node to be re-decided by the authoritative from-scratch Phase-A fixpoint, and whether that reconsideration condition can be represented as maintained execution state.
result_summary: HOLD. Reproduced the S025 first divergence exactly (ordos, seed 0, prefix 5, negateEvent:ev/vaela-invested; directChanged=[ev/vaela-invested]; 11-node reset closure; 3 divergent nodes). ROOT CAUSE A - a MISSING AUTHORITATIVE DEPENDENCY: fact/seal-held-vaela changed OUTSIDE the closure because it is a FACT whose truth comes from its VALIDITY WINDOW (validFrom/validTo via factNodeTruth), and the reverse index (supportGroups/enablesIn/excludes/invariant/precedes) OMITS validity-window edges. ROOT CAUSE B - STICKY ORDER-DEPENDENCE: ev/rite-of-binding-vaela and ev/succession-settled were INSIDE the reset closure but still diverged, decided TRUE using a stale member value before the member was re-decided (the sticky rule skips decided nodes). R \ closure = 51 over 800 prefixes (max 5 per prefix) - small and systematic. S021's aggregate remains exact; the dependency index is the gap. CLASSIFICATION: C - conditionally incremental. Minimum missing requirement: add fact validity-window edges to the reverse index and iterate to a fixpoint. Not validated. No incremental engine implemented.

answers.reconsidered_vs_changed: the from-scratch fixpoint evaluates every node (all start NEITHER) but only a few change; R (changed) is the right quantity and is small
answers.root_cause_a: the reverse-dependency index omits fact validity-window edges (validFrom/validTo -> fact node)
answers.root_cause_b: sticky order-dependence: nodes inside the closure can be decided with stale member values before the member is re-decided
answers.aggregate_exact: yes (S021) - the aggregate is not the failure
answers.decision_provenance_sufficient: previous decision + support evidence + current aggregate is sufficient ONLY if the index also carries validity-window edges and members are re-evaluated before dependents (or iterated to a fixpoint)
answers.ordering: the authoritative result is deterministic but schedule-sensitive; an incremental engine must preserve the schedule or iterate to a fixpoint after a sufficient reset

architectural_classification: C - conditionally incremental with an explicit dependency/order requirement
minimum_requirement: add fact validity-window (validFrom/validTo) edges to the reverse index, and iterate to a fixpoint after resetting the resulting closure
next_experiment: validate a validity-window-aware dependency index: add validFrom/validTo -> fact-node edges, reset the resulting closure, and re-run the S025 differential; if R \ closure reaches 0 the boundary is compact.
limitations: R used the judgment-changed definition; a stricter 're-evaluated and could have changed' definition is the whole model by construction.
Only 800 prefixes (20 histories x H=20 x 2 canons); no S024 synthetic corpus, no long horizon.
Ordering was analysed, not controlled (the schedule was not varied).
